opportunity.title: Survey-Based Research Platform and Platform Management Tool (RFI)
opportunity.description: The VA Acquisition Academy needs a Software as a Service survey-based research platform and platform management tool to securely collect responses to a competency survey it is piloting for acquisition human capital planning. Required: software subscriptions, maintenance and support. Period of performance is a 12-month base plus four 12-month options. Respondents provide a rough order of magnitude price against the salient characteristics by email by Oct 20, 2026.

profile._note: FICTIONAL SAMPLE COMPANY for scenario testing. Not a real firm. Past performance and staffing are invented; only the NAICS codes, set-aside definitions and every opportunity and award figure used against it are real public data.

profile.pastPerformance: Four years in the SBA 8(a) program. Two DoD sub-contracts for network monitoring (about $1.2M each) and one Air Force base-level help desk prime task order (about $900K).

verification: NAICS codes confirmed against USAspending reference (api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/references/naics) on 2026-10-16.
Set-asides follow SBA definitions: SBA = small business, 8A = 8(a) Business Development, HUBZONE, WOSB/EDWOSB, SDVOSB.

sources.title: Home - Acquisition Academy
sources.snippet:
The VA Acquisition Academy (VAAA) was created to address the growing acquisition workforce challenge facing the Department of Veterans Affairs and the Federal Government overall. With the downsizing from the last decade and the loss of institutional knowledge resulting from baby-boomer retirements, the acquisition workforce has been strained to keep pace with the increased amount of and complexities associated with outsourced work in support of the VA mission.

rationale.point: The opportunity is an RFI (Request for Information) for a SaaS survey-based research platform and management tool, not a solicitation; responding is low-cost but should align with demonstrated capabilities.

Lone Star Cyber's past performance consists of DoD network monitoring sub-contracts and an Air Force help desk task order, with no cited experience in SaaS platform development or survey-based research tools.

The opportunity has no set-aside (full and open competition) and the VA's award history in NAICS 541519 shows very large median awards (~$99M), suggesting any follow-on procurement may exceed the firm's current capacity (14 staff, 8 Secret clearances, facility clearance pending, FedRAMP not started).

risks: Low likelihood that RFI response leads to a near-term contract opportunity suited to the firm's size and experience.
Diverting limited proposal resources from more aligned pursuits.
No set-aside protection against large, established SaaS vendors.
nextSteps: Conduct a rapid internal gap analysis: does the firm have any SaaS platform, survey tool, or research management relevant experience (even commercial) that could be credibly presented?
If gaps are significant, consider a no-response decision and monitor for a future set-aside solicitation.
If responding, draft a concise capability statement highlighting any relevant software development, cloud/SaaS, or survey/analytics work, and note 8(a) eligibility for potential future set-asides.
